titulo.texto: Tubular Vessel from Alta Vista / Chalchihuites

frase_gancho.texto: A vessel in vivid colors, made almost exactly on the Tropic of Cancer.

puente_narrativo.texto: We continue northwest, to the most famous adobe city of the desert. Look for a round pot painted red and black on a cream background, which comes from Paquimé, in Chihuahua.

guion_corto.texto: This cylindrical vessel, about twelve centimeters tall, comes from Alta Vista, in Chalchihuites, Zacatecas, and was made between the years 600 and 900 of our era. It is decorated with a rare technique that archaeologists call pseudocloisonné: the surface was covered with a layer of stucco, designs were cut into it, and the hollows were filled with vivid colored pigments, such as red, yellow and turquoise. The result recalls the enamels of jewelers. Alta Vista was a city on the northern frontier of Mesoamerica, very close to the Tropic of Cancer. Colored minerals were extracted from its hills, and its inhabitants watched the sky with attention.

guion_largo.texto:
Imagine an invisible line: the northern frontier of Mesoamerica. Up to that point reached the peoples who planted maize, raised temples and traded like the ones you already know. Farther north, the desert began. But that line was not still. Farmers advanced northward when the rains allowed it, and Alta Vista was one of their most distant outposts. This vessel comes from that moving frontier.

The city lies almost exactly on the Tropic of Cancer, the northernmost line where the Sun stands directly overhead on the day of the summer solstice. It is thought that its builders observed the sky with great care: some of their constructions and alignments seem to mark the movements of the Sun. We do not know whether they knew the line as we do, but we do know that they knew how to look.

The region was rich in minerals, and its name tells the story. Chalchihuites comes from chalchihuitl, the Nahuatl word for the precious green stone. It is the same root as [Chalchiuhtlicue](mna_s04_chalchiuhtlicue), «she of the jade skirt», the water goddess you saw in the Teotihuacán Hall. From the hills of this region came green stones and red pigments, materials that the peoples of the center coveted.

Now take a look at the technique. Cloisonné is a French word that names a jewelry technique: fine metal partitions separate the colors of the enamel. Here there is no metal. The effect is achieved by cutting into the layer of stucco and filling the hollows with color, and that is why it is called pseudocloisonné, «false cloisonné». It is work of great precision: a single error in the cut is seen at once.

Among the motifs of these vessels appear stylized serpents, a symbol you have already seen from Teotihuacán to Tula. That tells us something important: Alta Vista did not live in isolation. Cities like this served as a bridge. They carried the desert's minerals south, and received ideas and objects from Mesoamerica. A frontier, at heart, is also a meeting place.

Around the year 900, and shortly after, the frontier retreated. It is thought that a drier period may have had an influence, along with political changes in the center of the country, and that the northern farmers withdrew toward the south or returned to more mobile ways of life. The details are still debated. But the story of Alta Vista reminds us that the line between Mesoamerica and the desert was never fixed.

Also in Zacatecas is La Quemada, another city of the frontier, with terraces, walls and a great hall of columns. Alta Vista and La Quemada can be visited today, and they tell the same story from two different places: that of peoples who dared to live on the edge.

A small vessel, the size of a large cup, can tell all of that. We do not know what was drunk from it, or on what occasion. But its color, its precision and its origin point to something special: a piece made to be seen.

texto: Look for the colors: red, yellow and turquoise
Observe the designs cut into the surface, as if they were enamel
Look at the cylindrical shape and the flat base

texto.Material: Clay (ceramic) decorated with the cloisonné or pseudocloisonné technique, pigments over lime plaster or lacquer

texto.pregunta: Myth: Mesoamerica ended at a fixed line, and farther north there was only empty desert.
texto.respuesta: Reality: The frontier moved. Farmers advanced and retreated according to the rains, and in places like Alta Vista people lived, traded and watched the sky.
